heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P handles Overture PETG natively out of the box with its stock direct drive extruder and stainless steel nozzle. Based on a safe volumetric flow limit of 14 mm³/s, this setup achieves reliable print speeds up to 167 mm/s without requiring an enclosure.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer filament settings to prevent under-extrusion at high print speeds.
Set Pressure Advance to 0.038 s (tune via OrcaSlicer PA line or pattern calibration) to eliminate corner bulging without severe stringing.
Enable 'Wipe while Retracting' with a wipe distance of 1.0 mm to cleanly detach tacky PETG melt from the stainless steel nozzle tip.
Set Aux Fan speed to 0% to avoid premature layer cooling, uneven shrinkage, and corner lifting on open-frame builds.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe fine stringing and nozzle whisker buildup
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Overture PETG is highly hygroscopic and absorbs ambient moisture rapidly, causing micro-boiling in the melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in an active filament dryer at 65°C for at least 6 hours, and lower printing temperature to 235°C-240°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Chunks torn from the PEI coating upon print removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically fuses to bare PEI surfaces due to high molecular affinity during thermal bonding.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVP glue stick or liquid glue to the Textured PEI sheet to serve as a separation barrier.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer split or poor mechanical z-adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or excessive auxiliary fan airflow freezing polymer chains before adequate molecular entanglement.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off the auxiliary fan completely, reduce part cooling fan to 20-40%, and raise nozzle temperature to 245°C.

faq.question: Can I print Overture PETG on the stock Bambu Lab P1P stainless steel nozzle?
faq.answer: Yes. Overture PETG is non-abrasive, meaning the stock 0.4mm stainless steel nozzle is fully compatible and will not suffer premature wear.

faq.question: Does the open-frame design of the P1P cause warping with Overture PETG?
faq.answer: PETG handles open-frame environments well, but you must keep the bed at 80°C and ensure the auxiliary cooling fan is disabled to prevent cold drafts.

faq.question: What max volumetric flow rate should I set for Overture PETG in OrcaSlicer?
faq.answer: Set the maximum volumetric flow rate to 14 mm³/s, which ensures reliable extrusion and caps standard layer speeds around 167 mm/s.

faq.question: Why is glue stick required if the P1P includes a textured PEI plate?
faq.answer: PETG adheres aggressively to PEI and can rip off fragments of the coating; glue acts as a sacrificial release agent rather than an adhesion promoter.
